out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Paper Towels Provided
violations.observation: Observed that paper towels were not provided at the employee restroom hand sink.
violations.corrective_action: Provide paper towels at each hand sink to allow employees to properly dry their hands after handwashing. CDI: PIC PLACED PAPER TOWELS AT THE HAND SINK.

out_items.name: Proper date marking and disposition

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: cooked chicken and beef with the production date and time.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. CDI: PIC HAS THE PRODUCTION DATE ON A LOG BUT NOT ON THE INDIVIDUALLY PACKAGED FOOD ITEMS. ENSURE ALL ITEMS HAVE THE PRODUCTION DATE AND TIME ON THEM.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Common Name, Working Containers
violations.observation: Working containers of poisonous and toxic materials are not properly labeled with a common name. OBSERVED CHEMICAL SPRAY BOTTLES NOT LABELED.
violations.corrective_action: Label all working containers of poisonous and toxic materials, including cleaners and sanitizers, with a common name to prevent the dangerous misuse of these materials. CDI: SPRAY BOTTLES WERE LABELED DURING THE INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Compliance with variance, specialized process, HACCP

violations.title: Food Establishmend Prohibited from ROP of Fish
violations.observation: The following fresh, not frozen, fish are packaged using the Reduced Oxygen Packaging (ROP) method: RAW SALMON IN ROP PACKAGING WITHOUT HEALTH DEPARTMENT APPROVAL.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment may not package fresh fish (raw, unfrozen) using a ROP method. CDI: THE SALMON WAS TAKEN OUT OF THE PACKAGING. DISCONTINUE ROP OF SALMON UNLESS APPROVED BY THE HEALTH DEPARTMENT.

out_items.name: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use

violations.title: Eating, Drinking, or Using Tobacco
violations.observation: Observed an open mug of tea being stored on the top of a food preparation table
violations.corrective_action: Food employees may have beverages in the kitchen areas as long as they are covered and consumed through a straw and stored in a manner that will prevent contamination to food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single service items. PIC MOVED THE MUG TO THE BACK TABLE OUT OF THE WAY OF FOOD PREPARATION

out_items.name: Hands clean and properly washed

violations.title: When to Wash
violations.observation: Observed PIC change tasks and change gloves multiple times without washing hands
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands OFTEN especially after handling trash, using the restroom, handling raw meats, handling soiled equipment and utensils, BEFORE putting on clean gloves, etc. Proper handwashing frequencies will aid in the reduction of foodborne illness. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO WASH HANDS FREQUENTLY. WASH HANDS BEFORE PUTTING GLOVES ON, AFTER TAKE TRASH OUT, AFTER TOUCHING BODY PARTS, HANDLING RAW PROTEINS, ETC. SEE WHEN TO WASH FACT SHEET.

out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: 1) in the 2DR lowboy cooler, Raw shrimp was observed being stored on top of RTE salad; 2) in the 2DR lowboy cooler, Raw eggs were observed being stored on top of mushroom soup
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. PIC MOVED ALL THE RAW PRODUCTS TO THE OTHER SIDE OF THE COOLER TO PREVENT CROSS CONTAMINATION. SEE PREVENTING CROSS CONTAMINATION FACT SHEET.

out_items.name: Proper cold holding temperatures

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: 1) in the 2DR lowboy cooler: mushroom soup (60f), split pea soup (53f)
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. PIC DISCARDED THE SOUPS

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: Upon discussion with PIC, soups are placed in the 2DR lowboy cooler while still warm.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC HOW TO PROPERLY COOL LARGE QUANTITIES OF SOUPS. SEE COOLING METHODS FACT SHEET.

out_items.name: In-use utensils properly stored

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: 1) ice cream scoop being stored in water
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. ICE CREAM SCOOP WAS TAKEN TO THE 3 COMPARTMENT SINK TO BE WASHED, RINSED, AND SANITIZED. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC TO KEEP SCOOP IN THE A DRY CONTAINER.

out_items.name: No bare hand contact with ready-to-eat food, or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed

violations.title: No Bare Hand Contact with RTE Foods
violations.observation: Observed PIC grab a baguette from the microwave with his bare hand.
violations.corrective_action: Except when washing fruits and vegetables, food employees may not contact ready-to-eat foods using their bare hands. Employees shall be using suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, or clean disposable gloves to handle all ready-to-eat foods. Proper handling of food and effective handwashing procedures will help prevent foodborne illness. PIC DISCARDED THE BREAD. EHS INSTRUCTED HIM TO USE TONGS OR GLOVED HANDS TO REMOVE BREAD FROM THE MICROWAVE.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Handwashing Sink, Designated Use
violations.observation: A homestyle water filter was observed attached to the handsink. During preparation of mushroom soup, EHS observed PIC use the water filter attached to the handsink to add water to the soup.
violations.corrective_action: Handsinks are to be used only for washing hands to encourage proper hand washing and to prevent contamination of cleaned hands. HAND SINKS ARE ONLY FOR HANDWASHING. PIC REMOVED THE WATER FILTER FROM THE HAND SINK.
